mathematics.independent_solution: Let u=AC=(-4,-4,9), v=BD=(-2,2,7), and alpha=arccos(63/sqrt(6441)). The four ray pairings have cosines +63/sqrt(6441), -63/sqrt(6441), -63/sqrt(6441), +63/sqrt(6441), hence exactly alpha and pi-alpha. Let beta=arccos(63/6441). Since 0<63/6441<63/sqrt(6441)<1 and arccos is strictly decreasing, 0<alpha<beta<pi/2. Therefore beta and pi-beta equal neither requested size.

option_checks.evidence: u.v=63 and ||u||||v||=sqrt(113*57)=sqrt(6441), not 6441. This option is beta; alpha<beta<pi/2 while pi-alpha>pi/2. It equals neither ray-angle size. The wrong denominator is the product of squared norms.
MA=-u/2 and MB=-v/2 give (MA.MB)/(||MA||||MB||)=63/sqrt(6441); MC=u/2 and MD=v/2 give the same. Their angle is alpha=arccos(63/sqrt(6441)).

This is pi-beta with beta=arccos(63/6441). Because alpha<beta<pi/2, pi/2<pi-beta<pi-alpha, so it is neither alpha nor pi-alpha. Supplementing an angle calculated with squared-norm normalization does not repair that error.
MA=-u/2 and MD=v/2 give cosine -63/sqrt(6441); MC=u/2 and MB=-v/2 do likewise. On [0,pi], arccos(-x)=pi-arccos(x), so their angle is pi-alpha.
